'''''Terminalia arjuna''''' is a tree of the [[genus]] ''[[Terminalia (plant)|Terminalia]]''. It is commonly known as '''arjuna'''<ref name=Biswas /> or '''arjun tree''' in English.<ref name=ecoindia /> It is used as a traditional [[medicinal plant]].<ref>{{cite Banglapedia |article=Flora |author=M Iqbal Zuberi}}</ref>

==Description==
''T. arjuna'' grows to about 20–25 metres tall; usually has a [[buttress roots|buttressed]] trunk, and forms a wide canopy at the crown, from which branches drop downwards. It has oblong, conical leaves which are green on the top and brown below; smooth, grey bark; it has pale yellow flowers which appear between March and June; its glabrous, 2.5 to 5 cm fibrous woody fruit, divided into five wings, appears between September and November.<ref name="Biswas">{{cite journal |last1=Biswas |first1=Moulisha |last2=Biswas |first2=Kaushik |last3=Karan |first3=Tarun K |last4=Bhattacharya |first4=Sanjib |last5=Ghosh |first5=Ashoke K |last6=Haldar |first6=Pallab K |year=2011 |title=Evaluation of analgesic and anti-inflammatory activities of ''Terminalia arjuna'' leaf |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/267427155_Evaluation_of_analgesic_and_anti-inflammatory_activities_of_Terminalia_arjuna_leaf |journal=Journal of Phytology |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=33–8}}</ref><ref name="ecoindia">{{cite web|url=http://www.ecoindia.com/flora/trees/arjun-tree.html|title=Arjun Tree |publisher=Eco India}}</ref>

The tree does not suffer from any major diseases or any deadly pest infestation, but it is susceptible to ''[[Phyllactinia terminale]]'' and rot due to ''[[polystictus affinis]]''.<ref name=CABI/>

==Distribution and habitat==
The arjuna is seen across the [[Indian subcontinent]], and usually found growing on river banks or near dry river beds in [[Uttar Pradesh]], [[Bihar]], [[Maharashtra]], [[Madhya Pradesh]], [[West Bengal]], [[Odisha]] and south and central [[India]], [[Karachi]] [[Pakistan]] along with [[Sri Lanka]] and [[Bangladesh]].<ref name=Biswas /><ref>{{cite book|last1=Rastogī|first1=Rekhā|title=Let Us Identify The Useful Trees(New)|date=2008|publisher=Children's Book Trust|page=7,8|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eL8RlQBNRjoC&dq=terminalia+arjuna&pg=PA7|isbn=978-81-7011-919-7}}</ref> It has also been planted in [[Malaysia]], [[Indonesia]] and [[Kenya]].<ref name=CABI>{{cite book|title=The CABI Encyclopedia of Forest Trees|year = 2013|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cBf4AgAAQBAJ&pg=PA464|page=464|isbn = 9781780642369}}</ref>

==Importance==

===Silk production===
The arjuna is one of the species whose leaves are fed on by the ''[[Antheraea paphia]]'' moth which produces the [[tassar silk]], a [[wild silk]] of commercial importance.<ref name="fao">{{cite web|url=http://www.fao.org/docrep/005/ab598e/AB598E13.htm|title=Non-wood forest products In 15 countries of Tropical Asia|author=M.P. Shiva|publisher=Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations}}</ref> 
<!--[[File:Terminalia_arjuna_trunk_03_by_Line1.JPG|thumb|left|[[Buttress root]]s and bark.]]-->

===Ecology===
The arjuna is considered a [[keystone species]] in riparian forests of southern India, providing nesting habitat for species including [[Indian giant squirrel|Malabar giant squirrels]] and critically endangered [[White-rumped vulture|white-rumped vultures]]. Dead trunks host termites, which in turn feed [[sloth bear|sloth bears]].<ref>{{cite journal | journal=Journal of Wildlife Science | title=Status and ecological significance of Terminalia arjuna (Roxb.) Wight & Arn., a keystone species in the riparian forest of Moyar River valley in Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, Southern India. | last=Sekar | first=Iyanar |last2=Vedagiri |first2=Thirumurugan | display-authors=etal | url=https://jwls.in/rkvl6975/ | date=2025 }}</ref>
